evidence: AgentManifest.access requires local Ollama agents to be private and owner-only.
Edge runtime proxy forwards x-agent-caller-scope=public, so public calls cannot select owner-only local agents without a future authenticated owner scope.
Runtime chat, sequential orchestration, and Queen workflow selection reject owner-only agents for public callers.
importantNodes.boundary: Authenticated owner scope is a follow-up integration point; current public Preview intentionally cannot operate the user's local Ollama agents.

evidence: rankAgentCandidates deduplicates ranked candidates by modelTag.
Task match UI filters default public candidates to public-market agents and keeps only one candidate per modelTag.
Sequential orchestration UI blocks adding a second agent with the same model tag.
importantNodes.boundary: Persistent post-task score writeback is planned; current ranking supports score inputs and exploration/retirement policy but does not yet persist new scores to a production database.

evidence: AgentCandidate carries tags and license metadata for ranking explanations.
Ranking reasons include model-pool-draw, tag/license metadata, new-model exploration, new-model protection, and low-score old-model retirement.
New zero-score models can enter exploration without pretending to have historical quality.
importantNodes.boundary: Real score deltas after completion still need durable writeback and anti-gaming checks before being marked verified.

evidence: @mastra/core and @langchain/langgraph are installed in the local-agent-runner workspace package.

Mastra registers the top-level Queen workflow container and LangGraph compiles/invokes the internal state graph boundary.
importantNodes.boundary: Existing Agent Market GraphQL remains the product protocol; this is a controlled internal rewrite, not a full platform migration.
